Effects on the liver. Vigabatrin has demonstrated in-vivo and in-vitro inhibition of plasma-alanine transaminase activity, which may mask signs of early underlying hepatic disease if only transaminase levels are evaluated.1 1. Richens A, et al. Evidence for both in vivo and in vitro interac- tion between vigabatrin and alanine transaminase. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1997; 43: 163–8. Effects on mental function. Behavioural disturbances rang- ing from irritability and confusion to psychotic reactions have been reported in patients receiving vigabatrin.1-7 An analysis8 of adverse effect reports from double-blind controlled studies found that the incidence of psychotic reactions was about 2.5% in viga- batrin-treated patients; however, the most common psychiatric reaction was depression, which occurred in 8 to 12% of patients. Symptoms of psychiatric disturbance were often relatively mild. Psychiatric reactions are generally reversible when doses are re- duced or gradually stopped. In 2 patients9,10 psychosis developed after sudden withdrawal of vigabatrin; mental state improved when the drug was reinstated.
